title: PROPERTY_USAGE_ARRAY does not respect "const" flag in class_name correctly
body: ### Tested versions 4.6 latest stable ### System information Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9159) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-11700K @ 3.60GHz (16 threads) - 31.83 GiB memory ### Issue description Hello, i tried to set up an array with given items in a Resource. The array may not add or remove items, but the items shall be allowed to be dragged/reordered. What I understand from the docs of `PROPERTY_USAGE_ARRAY`: ``` - static: The elements can't be re-arranged. - const: New elements can't be added. ``` So, for my understanding, i need to specify "static" explicitly to avoid reordering. In other words, specifying "const" only _should_ allow reordering. The `unfoldable` flag is also not respected. The array always is collapsed. Here's how I did the setup of the array: ```gdscript func _get_property_list() -> Array[Dictionary]: var properties: Array[Dictionary] = [] properties.append({ "name": "columns", "type": TYPE_ARRAY, "hint": PROPERTY_HINT_TYPE_STRING, "hint_string": "%d/%d:%s" % [TYPE_OBJECT, PROPERTY_HINT_RESOURCE_TYPE, "ApiLobbyHeaderColumn"], "usage": PROPERTY_USAGE_DEFAULT | PROPERTY_USAGE_ARRAY, "class_name": "ApiLobbyHeader,columns/,swap_method=_switch_index,const,unfoldable" }) for i in range(columns.size()): properties.append({ "name": "columns/%d" % i, "type": TYPE_OBJECT, "hint": PROPERTY_HINT_RESOURCE_TYPE, "hint_string": "Resource", "usage": PROPERTY_USAGE_DEFAULT }) return properties ``` All functionality works fine, even saving/loading but no reorder-grips are shown. Even the child resource is working fine. I did a "button" workaround in there to reorder items but this is ugly in two ways: optical and for the user experience. ### Steps to reproduce - Open the attached demo project - double-click the "DemoScene" in the file system to open the scene - click on the root node - now look in the inspector -> you see the "header" resource - expand it -> you see the item list of 5 pre-filled items - no reorder grips ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [array-reorder-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25010461/array-reorder-bug.zip)
